messages:
mike-r: FYI ran a smoke today — small-batch multi-model tenant started hitting a 2.5x p99 token latency regression when KV cache hit rate jumped. profile uploaded: https://artifacts/reports/1719007654/profile.html :frowning:

infra-bot: profiling artifact uploaded by @mike-r: https://artifacts/reports/1719007654/profile.html

sylvie: thanks — quick question: is this only for 2-model co-residency or also seen with 3+?

mike-r: only repro so far with 2 models sharing a single A10. 3-model test weirdly fell back to lower throughput but not the latency spike.

kevin: can you paste the allocator / workspace config you used? suspect the slab soft-reserve scoring is letting KV cache evict critical workspace buffers on kernel fallback.

mike-r: config snippet below — this is the test harness we used:
```json
{
  "allocator": "soft-slab-v2",
  "soft_reserve_pct": 0.12,
  "evict_order": ["inactive_kv", "scratch", "workspace"],
  "workspace_target_mb": 1024,
  "kv_prefetch": true
}
```

raj: if evict_order prefers inactive_kv ahead of workspace, that explains cache churn — when kernel selection falls back to slower kernels we spike secondary allocations and fragmentation. suggest switching to evict_order ["scratch","workspace","inactive_kv"] for a canary.

nina: also saw a pattern in the flamegraph: multiple small kernel launches (recompile fallback) back-to-back. could be kernel selector preferring fused kernels until context size increases. we should bias selector to stable kernels under high co-residency.

kevin: agree. two quick experiments: 1) increase workspace_target_mb from 1024->1536; 2) adjust kernel_selector config to prefer non-fallback kernels when concurrent_residents >= 2. both should reduce transient alloc pressure.

mike-r: kicked off experiment 1 and 2 on staging with the same traffic profile. linking logs: https://logs/stage/1719007654/exp-1 and exp-2.

infra-bot: experiment run started by @mike-r: exp-1 (workspace 1536), exp-2 (selector bias). will post completion.

sylvie: ping when done — if that improves p99 we still need a longer-term fix: allocator should be kv-aware and avoid evicting entries used in next-window prefetch. maybe maintain a short LRU prediction window keyed by request traces.

raj: we have a prototype 'kv-hotset' metric in perf agent. can wire that into eviction scoring: give active_kv an ephemeral protection score for N seconds after access. low-effort patch.

nina: also add a batching heuristic tweak: when co-resident_count >1 and avg_seq_len < 128, favor smaller batch targets to limit workspace growth bursts. that plus kv-hotset might keep swaps minimal.

mike-r: first results in — exp-1 (larger workspace) removed the p99 spike, exp-2 (selector-bias) reduced kernel fallback occurrence by ~60%. combined run shows stable p99 within SLA. profiling diffs uploaded: https://artifacts/reports/1719007654/combined-diff.html

kevin: awesome. next steps: 1) land allocator scoring change (kv-hotset protection) behind flag, 2) add selector bias tuning param, 3) add batcher heuristic switch for co-residency. can we target a small PR for each?

mike-r: I'll open 3 PRs today. tagging @sylvie for review on allocator scoring.

sylvie: I'll review. also let's add an e2e test that simulates KV-hit bursts + kernel fallback to prevent regressions.

raj: I'll wire kv-hotset metric into perf agent telemetry so we can dashboard protection efficacy.

infra-bot: experiment run completed: all artifacts uploaded to https://artifacts/reports/1719007654/ (logs, profiles, diff).

mike-r: thanks all. leaving the thread open for follow-ups, but good to close the immediate perf regression case. :thumbsup:
